html:
SMTO-EXE-0110 — SMTO isn't set up to connect to your existing browser

GUID: 08e15978-1f2c-5a6e-b924-919072c07188
Slug: browser-attach-not-configured
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to connect to a browser that is already open on the computer, but that computer's Gateway has not been set up to allow it. SMTO did not connect to or change any browser.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you don't need your already-open browser, ask SMTO: "Start your own browser session instead." SMTO can always open its own separate browser without any extra setup.
  2. If SMTO must use your open browser, for example where you're already signed in, ask the person who manages the Gateway to allow browser connection on it. Connecting to an existing browser is off by default. Only the administrator of the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work on a computer) can turn it on.
  3. Don't paste a browser connection address or debugging port into the chat, and don't turn on browser debugging yourself. That address gives full control of the browser, so it must be set up privately on the Gateway, not shared in chat.

What success looks like

  • SMTO either works in its own new browser, or connects to your browser and shows its open tabs.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't export or share your browser's cookies, passwords or saved data as a workaround.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway refused a browser attach because GATEWAY_BROWSER_ALLOW_ATTACH is not enabled, GATEWAY_BROWSER_CDP_ENDPOINT is not set, or the browser_attach_cdp capability is not reported.

What this means

  • Browser attachment was requested without both operator-approved attachment enablement and a configured CDP endpoint, or the requested attachment capability was absent. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Browser attachment was requested without both operator-approved attachment enablement and a configured CDP endpoint, or the requested attachment capability was absent.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect operator-owned attachment settings and browser.status without scanning ports or exposing the private endpoint.

How to fix it

  • Attach requires both GATEWAY_BROWSER_ALLOW_ATTACH=true and GATEWAY_BROWSER_CDP_ENDPOINT in the selected Gateway's process environment (the endpoint is a secret and is never a tool argument); without them readiness omits browser_attach_cdp and BrowserService rejects attach/detach. Set both deliberately, restart the Gateway after active work finishes, and confirm browser.status lists browser_attach_cdp. Never scan ports or enable remote debugging automatically.
  • An operator must explicitly set GATEWAY_BROWSER_ALLOW_ATTACH and GATEWAY_BROWSER_CDP_ENDPOINT on the selected Gateway. Do not scan ports or enable debugging automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • An operator must explicitly set GATEWAY_BROWSER_ALLOW_ATTACH and GATEWAY_BROWSER_CDP_ENDPOINT on the selected Gateway. Do not scan ports or enable debugging automatically.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended approved endpoint is configured and the owning attachment flow succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
